record.paper_title: Toward epidemic thresholds on temporal networks: a review and open questions
record.original_question: Temporal contact patterns may be periodic because of seasonal or other recurring changes in behavior and social interaction. What effect do such periodic contact patterns have on disease spreading and epidemic thresholds in temporal networks?

evidence.quote: Contacts may also exhibit periodic patterns, e.g., due to seasonal changes in behavior and social interaction (Enright and Kao, 2018).

The effect this has on disease spreading has not been explicitly examined in temporal networks, though most temporal network models appear to be capable of extension by simply repeating the time period.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a temporal network model in which the contact structure is described by a time-indexed sequence of graphs $\{G_t\}_{t \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}}$ on a fixed vertex set $V$ of $n$ nodes, where each $G_t = (V, E_t)$ specifies which pairs of nodes are in contact at discrete time $t$. Assume the sequence is periodic with period $T \geq 1$, i.e. $G_{t+T} = G_t$ for all $t \geq 0$. On this temporal network, run a susceptible–infected–susceptible (SIS) (or SIR) Markovian spreading process: at each time step $t$, an infected node infects each susceptible neighbor in $G_t$ independently with probability $\beta \in (0,1]$, and each infected node recovers independently with probability $\mu \in (0,1]$. Define the epidemic threshold as the critical ratio $(\beta/\mu)_c$ above which the expected number of infected nodes does not vanish in the long-time limit (equivalently, the spectral threshold characterizing the stability of the disease-free state under the periodic time-inhomogeneous dynamics).

Problem. Determine the effect of the periodicity $T$ and the structure of the periodic sequence $\{G_t\}_{t=0}^{T-1}$ on the epidemic threshold $(\beta/\mu)_c$ and on the qualitative behavior of disease spread. In particular:

(a) Derive an analytical expression (or sharp bounds) for $(\beta/\mu)_c$ as a function of $T$ and of the sequence of adjacency matrices $A_0, A_1, \dots, A_{T-1}$, for example in terms of the spectral radius of the product $\prod_{t=0}^{T-1}\big((1-\mu) I + \beta A_t\big)$ or an analogous operator capturing one full period.

(b) Identify how the threshold compares with that of (i) the time-aggregated static network with adjacency $\bar A = \tfrac{1}{T}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1} A_t$, and (ii) a randomly shuffled (non-periodic) version of the same sequence, and characterize regimes in which periodicity raises or lowers the threshold.

(c) Determine whether resonance phenomena can occur between the period $T$ of the contact pattern and the intrinsic time scale $1/\mu$ of the recovery process, and quantify their impact on outbreak size and on the prevalence in the endemic state.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent reviews and research on epidemic spreading on temporal networks (including the 2019/2021 review on epidemic thresholds and the 2021 Royal Society Interface review on concurrency measures) note that periodic/seasonal contact patterns have not been explicitly analyzed for their effect on epidemic thresholds in temporal networks, although standard temporal network models can in principle be extended to periodic settings. Analytical thresholds exist for some time-varying models (e.g., Valdano et al., Phys. Rev. X 2015), but a systematic theory specifically addressing periodic/seasonal contact structure and its impact on the threshold remains undeveloped.

status_evidence.title: Toward epidemic thresholds on temporal networks: a review and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: The effect this has on disease spreading has not been explicitly examined in temporal networks, though most temporal network models appear to be capable of extension by simply repeating the time period.
status_evidence.claim: The effect of periodic contact patterns on epidemic thresholds in temporal networks has not been explicitly examined.

status_evidence.title: Analytical Computation of the Epidemic Threshold on Temporal Networks
status_evidence.snippet: Analytical derivation of the epidemic threshold in terms of the spectral radius of a matrix encoding both network structure and disease dynamics for general temporal networks.
status_evidence.claim: General-purpose spectral threshold formulas exist for temporal networks but are not specialized to periodic/seasonal structure.

status_evidence.title: Concurrency measures in the era of temporal network epidemiology: a review
status_evidence.snippet: Review of how temporal contact structures, including periodic and bursty patterns, may influence spreading; full theoretical understanding remains limited.
status_evidence.claim: A complete theoretical understanding of how periodicity influences epidemic thresholds in temporal networks is still lacking.
